insight: For New Zealand in the FIFA World Cup 2026, hydration breaks have had a mixed impact on their momentum. When they were pressing before a break, they tended to lose momentum, with an average change of -0.100 per minute, and were only able to maintain their momentum once out of three times. In contrast, when they weren't pressing before a break, they actually gained momentum, with an average change of +0.033 per minute, suggesting that the breaks gave them a chance to regroup and refocus. Overall, New Zealand's performance after hydration breaks has been somewhat inconsistent, but it seems that taking a break can be beneficial for them when they're not already applying heavy pressure on their opponents.
